failures.criterion: A gone client is logged 499 (review 2, PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6yULld): a client that leaves while queued in admission
failures.evidence: Real binary at 1176657a (gone.sh, stack issue LGA-2, issues table locked 8 s so 24 comment writes hold the write units): a comment POST whose client closed 0.4 s into its queue wait was logged 'method=POST ... user_agent=probe-gone status=429 elapsed_ms=1001 bytes=135', the same as the pre-fix tree 36ca438e ('status=429 elapsed_ms=1000'); a GET closed the same way was logged status=499 at the head (status=200 bytes=0 pre-fix). net/http notices a closed connection only once the body has been read, and a queued write's body has not been, so the request keeps its queue slot for the whole wait and a refusal is written to a client that has gone. The implementer's TestARequestWhoseClientLeavesWhileItIsQueuedIsLoggedClientGone cancels the context directly, so it does not catch this. Red test: packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/request_bounds_test.go TestAQueuedWriteWhoseClientHangsUpIsLoggedClientGone (commit 0e2b3ea9), a real httptest.Server connection closed while queued. `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=... go test -p 1 -count=1 -v ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestAQueuedWriteWhoseClientHangsUpIsLoggedClientGone$'` fails at the head: 'the queued write whose client hung up left the queue 10.003240775s later and logged: ... status=429 elapsed_ms=10001 bytes=135 want status=499'. The same test made into a GET (throwaway control) passes in 0.68 s.

failures.criterion: The PR body's named risk 'Refusal p99 ... writes 1.1-1.3 s' matches the head
failures.evidence: t12-head-10x-a and -b: write refusals (all 429 OVERLOADED, 6,294 and 6,271) p50 1,047.6 ms, p90 1,978.6 and 1,985.7 ms, p99 2,126 and 2,157 ms, max 5,791 and 5,283 ms; read refusals p99 488 and 355 ms. Since 0647b935 a write parks its admission units at its body's first read whether or not the body has already arrived (body_drain.go:278, drainedBody.Read calls park before every first read) and Ticket.Resume takes them back through acquire, at the back of the queue (admission.go:342-362), so under load a write can wait for room twice: once to be admitted and once to resume, and be refused after it was admitted. This contradicts the risk line and the admission.go DefaultWait comment ('a refusal's p99 is about the wait'). A deterministic red test was not written: with every write carrying a body each park hands the unit on and each resume gets it back in order (my throwaway TestAWriteAdmittedWithItsBodyInHandKeepsItsUnits passed 3 of 3 at the head); the double wait shows only under a full queue. The architect decides between parking only a body still arriving and restating the risk with these numbers.
